column3: NKJV has “one thing,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “a word.”
Close to the Greek; “farmers” is rendered “vinedressers.”
NKJV includes “when they see him,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
NKJV includes “Come,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “let us kill him.”
NKJV has “the chief priests and the scribes,” the order of the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “the scribes and the chief priests.”
Close to the Greek; “tribute” is rendered “taxes.”
NKJV includes “Why do you test Me?,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “He said to them.”
NKJV has “They answered and said,” following the Textus Receptus wording; the critical text reads “they said.”
NKJV has “took her as wife, and he died childless,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “and the second.”
